findings.issue_text: [BUG] The public findMany method is deleted in this diff while the diff contains no updates to any of its call sites elsewhere in the codebase. Any remaining caller (e.g. insights API routes previously calling service.findMany) fails TypeScript compilation with 'Property findMany does not exist on type InsightsBookingService', breaking the build; the diff assumes without evidence that no callers exist.

[ADVISORY] The entire 'Caching' describe block is deleted while the caching logic it covered (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions in getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions) remains in insightsBooking.ts. A future regression in the memoization (e.g. re-declaring the cache field, or clearing it per call) produces repeated authorization queries per request and no test fails; the staff cost is silent perf/behavior drift in the insights hot path.

[ADVISORY] The new InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions type makes teamId optional for all scopes, replacing the zod discriminated union (insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema) as the constructor's accepted type, which required teamId for scope:'team'. Callers can now type-check passing scope:'team' without teamId; the code silently returns NOTHING_CONDITION from buildTeamAuthorizationCondition instead of surfacing a validation error, so misconfigured dashboard requests render as empty data rather than failing loudly.

[ADVISORY] getBaseConditions contains dead branches: authConditions is typed Promise<Prisma.Sql> and is never null/undefined (buildAuthorizationConditions returns NOTHING_CONDITION as fallback), so the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches are unreachable. Readers must reason about a three-branch combination path where only the first two cases can ever execute, and the dead NOTHING fallback suggests a 'no conditions' case that actually cannot occur through this method, misleading future edits that rely on it.

[BUG] The public findMany method is deleted with no replacement, breaking every existing caller that invoked InsightsBookingService.findMany. Any call site (e.g. insights routers/route handlers that did service.findMany({select, where, take})) now hits a missing method: TypeScript compile failure in-tree, or runtime TypeError for out-of-tree/dynamic callers; consumers must each re-implement pagination/ordering as raw SQL, and the diff shows no consumer migration.

[BUG] buildOrgAuthorizationCondition emits ("teamId" = ANY($1)) with an empty array parameter when the org has no child teams, which Postgres cannot type-infer. When findAllByParentId returns [], the generated Prisma.sql contains = ANY($1) bound to a JS empty array; Prisma serializes it as an untyped empty array literal and Postgres raises 'cannot determine type of empty array', turning the whole insights query into a 500 instead of the previous safe empty result (old code used teamId:{in:[]} which Prisma handles).

[BUG] The new InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions type drops the discriminated-union guarantee, so options can be {scope:'team'} with teamId undefined and still typecheck. A caller constructing the service with scope:'team' and no teamId passes the compiler; at runtime findByIdAndParentId({id: options.teamId}) receives undefined and the resulting Prisma query throws or silently matches nothing, where the previous InsightsBookingServiceOptions union (still exported and still used by buildOrgAuthorizationCondition/buildTeamAuthorizationCondition) rejected this shape at compile time.

[BUG] The Caching describe block is deleted but the caching mechanism (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions) remains in production code, removing all verification of cache behavior. A regression that re-fetches authorization conditions on every getAuthorizationConditions() call (e.g. the cache-check rewritten to assign before early-return) would no longer be caught by any test, silently reintroducing N+1 membership/team lookups per insights request; the deleted tests were the only assertions that the second call returns the cached conditions.

[ADVISORY] buildTeamAuthorizationCondition omits the isTeamBooking:false branch when userIdsFromTeam is empty, but buildOrgAuthorizationCondition keeps its team branch even when teamIds is empty, leaving the two symmetric builders with divergent empty-set handling. The next maintainer adding a scope or copying one builder as a template inherits inconsistent assumptions about which branches are safe to drop, and the empty-teamIds org path (single ANY([]) condition) is exactly the branch whose behavior was not audited.

[BUG] The diff deletes the only public data-access method findMany(), so the PR title's 'convert to raw queries' actually removes the service's query capability and pushes raw SQL composition onto every out-of-tree caller. Every existing consumer that called service.findMany(...) now gets a compile error or, worse, must hand-write `SELECT ... WHERE ${baseConditions}` raw SQL per call site, duplicating table/column knowledge outside the service; this work is not traceable to the stated intent and expands scope across the codebase.

[ADVISORY] New exported type InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions (userId and orgId unconditionally required, teamId optional) is added without any requirement, and it silently replaces the validated InsightsBookingServiceOptions as the constructor input. The zod discriminated union insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema (lines 8-26) is now dead at this call path: callers can pass options that violate the union (e.g. scope 'team' with no teamId, orgId: undefined at runtime) and the service will build SQL against undefined values instead of failing validation.

[ADVISORY] Constructing the raw-SQL fragments inside getBaseConditions couples every caller to the exact table name and quoted column identifiers of BookingTimeStatusDenormalized, an invariant the service previously encapsulated via Prisma's typed where-input. Any future caller composing getBaseConditions() into a raw query must know the physical column names ("isTeamBooking", "eventParentId") and table name; a rename or dialect change (this SQL is Postgres-specific with = ANY) breaks every call site at runtime instead of compile time.

[ADVISORY] The entire 'Caching' describe block is deleted, removing all coverage for the caching behavior that still exists in the service (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions memoization in insightsBooking.ts). A regression that breaks memoization (e.g. re-querying on every getAuthorizationConditions call, doubling DB round-trips per request) would pass CI silently; the behavior survives in production code but has no test.

[ADVISORY] The MembershipRole.array.includes check is rewritten to === comparisons with no requirement driving it — unrelated refactoring bundled into a raw-query conversion PR. Behavior is equivalent today, but the churn makes it harder to attribute this diff's intent in review/git-blame; if MembershipRole gains case variants the explicit === pair silently excludes them where includes() would have kept parity visible.

[ADVISORY] getBaseConditions falls back to NOTHING_CONDITION when both inputs are null, changing the former semantics where an empty AND array meant 'no restriction'. Currently unreachable as a behavior change (buildAuthorizationConditions never returns null), but the branch encodes deny-by-default for a state that previously meant permissive; if a future scope returns null to mean 'unrestricted', this silently returns zero rows instead.

[BUG] Prisma.sql expands interpolated arrays into a comma-separated parameter list, so `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))` renders as `= ANY($1, $2, $3)` which is invalid Postgres syntax, crashing every org/team-scope query with more than one member/team. The first org or team-scope insights request with 2+ teams/users throws a raw-query syntax error and returns a 500; the single-element integration test never exercises the multi-element path, so CI stays green.

[BUG] The toEqual assertions compare Prisma.Sql fragments by string content, but the production code parameterizes `isTeamBooking` (rendering `$2`) while the tests expect the literal `= true`, and the combined-condition test writes filter-AND-auth in an order the code emits as auth-AND-filter, so the assertions cannot match. These test cases fail as written (or force a meaningless string-diff rewrite), so the suite does not actually verify the generated authorization SQL against a real query — a stand-in guard that validates textual form, not behavior.

[BUG] The public method findMany was deleted and the return types of getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions changed from Prisma WhereInput to Prisma.Sql, breaking every existing caller that composed or executed these conditions via the Prisma client. Any call site outside this diff still calling service.findMany or passing the conditions to prisma.bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany now fails at type-check or, worse, receives a Prisma.Sql object a Prisma `where` cannot interpret, silently filtering nothing when duck-typed.

[ADVISORY] The new InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions type replaces the zod-discriminated union at the constructor boundary, making userId and orgId required for every scope and dropping runtime validation of options entirely. A caller constructing the service with scope 'team' but no userId/orgId, or with an unvalidated string scope, no longer fails validation; the zod schema is retained but nothing enforces it, so the next caller passes malformed options that surface as a broken authorization condition instead of a 4xx.

[ADVISORY] The service now emits hand-written, Postgres-dialect raw SQL with quoted camelCase identifiers, coupling the service to (a) the exact physical column names of BookingTimeStatusDenormalized and (b) Postgres-specific constructs (ANY), removing the database-agnostic and schema-map-safe layer Prisma previously provided. Any future column rename, @map, or driver change silently breaks every authorization query at runtime rather than at type-check; a staff reviewer should weigh whether raw SQL is needed here at all, since the previous WhereInput expressed the same conditions.

[ADVISORY] buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition duplicate the same team-booking/user-booking OR-arm construction with hand-rolled reduce-based joining, a pattern now copied three times across the file (org, team, filter). The next condition variant (e.g. a third OR arm or a parenthesization fix) must be applied in three places; the drift already shows as inconsistent parenthesization between the org and filter reducers, and a precedence mistake in one copy is exactly the kind of authorization bug raw SQL invites.

[BUG] The public exported method findMany was deleted and replaced by getBaseConditions, removing the only documented way callers consumed this service (Prisma findMany args API) without any adapter keeping the old call signature. Every existing caller of InsightsBookingService.findMany (routing/UI data layers not in this diff) fails to compile or, for dynamically-typed call sites, silently gets no data — the PR's stated intent was 'convert to Prisma.sql raw queries', but the iteration quietly changed the objective to a public API removal, an objective change with no explicit human acceptance recorded in the diff.

[ADVISORY] The new hand-written InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions type duplicates the existing zod discriminated union insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema instead of deriving from it (z.infer), and the constructor silently switched its accepted type from the validated InsightsBookingServiceOptions to this parallel type. Two sources of truth for the options contract: when the zod schema is next tightened or a scope gains/loses a required field (e.g. teamId), this type drifts silently; worse, the constructor no longer receives the zod-validated type, so unvalidated option shapes now flow into buildAuthorizationConditions where an unrecognized shape falls through to the else branch returning NOTHING_CONDITION — the user silently sees an empty insights dashboard instead of a 4xx validation error.

[ADVISORY] The entire Caching describe block (both the authorization-conditions cache test and the filter-conditions cache test) was deleted even though the caching implementation (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions in insightsBooking.ts) was retained. The cache behavior is now completely untested: a regression that re-queries conditions per call (or caches stale conditions across filter changes) would pass CI; deleting tests that guard still-present behavior is an objective change (from 'verify caching' to 'drop caching verification') that no human acceptance is recorded for.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten assertions compare getAuthorizationConditions output against the exact Prisma.sql fragment the implementation builds, string-for-string including quoting and ANY() formatting, rather than asserting any semantic property. The tests are now tautological mirrors of the implementation: any harmless refactor (reordering parentheses, changing ANY-array serialization, renaming quoting style) breaks five tests with no behavioral change, while a real authorization bug that is consistently reflected in both implementation and expected-SQL literal (e.g. swapping isTeamBooking true/false) passes CI — the previous Prisma-where-object assertions at least encoded intent independently of serialization.

[ADVISORY] The final else branch of getBaseConditions returning NOTHING_CONDITION is dead code: getAuthorizationConditions is typed Promise<Prisma.Sql> (non-nullable) and always returns a fragment, so authConditions is never null and the 'both null' path can never execute. It also silently encodes a semantic that differs from the removed findMany, where authConditions was unconditionally ANDed and an empty AND array meant 'no restriction'; a future reader extending filter nullability could rely on this branch believing 'both absent = see nothing' when the historical intent for absent auth was never defined here.

[ADVISORY] The entire 'Caching' describe block (both cache tests) was deleted from the test file while the caching logic (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions memoization in insightsBooking.ts getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions) remains in the implementation, so the cache behavior is no longer asserted anywhere in this diff. A future regression that breaks or removes memoization (e.g., re-querying memberships on every call, or returning a stale/wrong cached condition) passes the suite silently; previously the deleted 'should cache authorization conditions'/'should cache filter conditions' tests caught this by calling the getter twice and asserting the second result equaled the first.

[ADVISORY] The org-scope and team-scope authorization tests verify the produced SQL only by string-mirror equality against a hand-copied duplicate of the implementation's template literal, and never execute it — the ONLY test that runs the conditions through prisma.$queryRaw (the renamed getBaseConditions test) exercises solely the scope:'user' path, so the `("userId" = ANY(${[...]}))` / `("teamId" = ANY(${[...]}))` constructs are never executed against Postgres. If Prisma's sql tag expands the passed array into multiple placeholders (its documented behavior for arrays, producing `ANY($1, $2, ...)` which is invalid Postgres syntax — correct usage is a single array param or Prisma.join), every org- and team-scoped Insights query would crash at runtime with a syntax/prepared-statement error, while these tests still pass because the test's mirrored template produces the identical (broken) SQL string; the mirror also means any precedence bug duplicated in both the impl and the test literal is invisible.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten scope:'user' assertion compares against a template literal duplicated from the implementation rather than querying with the conditions, so it verifies textual identity, not filter semantics. A change that alters parameter binding (e.g., binding the wrong column order or swapping userId/teamId values) that happens to produce identical text in both copies passes; the semantic guarantee now rests entirely on the single getBaseConditions raw-execution test, which covers only this one scope's shape.

[ADVISORY] The getBaseConditions test suite in this diff covers only the both-conditions-present path; the new else-branches in getBaseConditions (filter-only, and both-null returning NOTHING_CONDITION) are never triggered by any test in the diff. A regression in the branch selection (e.g., returning null instead of NOTHING_CONDITION when both are null, causing the raw WHERE clause to receive a non-SQL value and the $queryRaw to fail or match nothing) would not be caught; previously the filter-less caching test at least exercised the filter-null path through the old findMany.

[ADVISORY] Neither org-scope test covers the empty-list branches the implementation explicitly guards (userIdsFromOrg.length === 0 in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition, userIdsFromTeam.length === 0 in buildTeamAuthorizationCondition), even though the diff restructured exactly those branches. If the empty-list guard is dropped or mis-edited (e.g., the condition pushed unconditionally with an empty array), tests still pass because every fixture populates members; the resulting SQL (`userId = ANY(empty)` matching no personal bookings vs. previously `userId: {in: []}` semantics) is unverified against real data.

[BUG] buildOrgAuthorizationCondition unconditionally emits `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))` even when teamIds is empty, producing invalid/untyped empty-array SQL where the old `{ teamId: { in: [] } }` was a valid always-false condition. An org whose orgId has no child teams (or where findAllByParentId returns empty) causes the Prisma raw query to fail at runtime with a Postgres parameter-type/ARRAY error instead of returning zero rows, turning an authorized-but-empty org into a 500 on every insights request.

[ADVISORY] Constructor parameter type changed from the zod-validated InsightsBookingServiceOptions to a hand-written InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions structurally looser than the discriminated union, and the schema is never parsed at the boundary. Callers can now pass { scope: "team", userId, orgId } with a undefined/wrongly-typed teamId through type-asserted call sites; buildTeamAuthorizationCondition then interpolates undefined into `("teamId" = ${options.teamId})`, yielding `"teamId" = NULL` which matches no rows — an authorization condition that silently returns NOTHING instead of failing fast at the boundary.

[ADVISORY] The only test asserting cached conditions behave identically across repeat calls was deleted while the caching fields cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions remain live logic. A future regression in the memoization (e.g. caching a null filter then never rebuilding when filters change) would be invisible; this diff removed the only guard while keeping the mechanism, making the next change to buildFilterConditions riskier.

[BUG] buildTeamAuthorizationCondition interpolates userIdsFromTeam directly into `("userId" = ANY(${userIdsFromTeam}))` with the empty case only guarded by the if, so the non-empty path with a single-element list is fine but the corresponding Prisma.sql fragment template is duplicated from buildOrgAuthorizationCondition with inverted AND/OR logic — drift between the two copies (AND for org, OR join wrapper) is already present and one wrong edit flips authorization scope. The parallel hand-maintained raw-SQL builders mean the next authorization change (e.g. adding a role filter) must be edited in two places with opposite boolean joins; a mistake silently widens or narrows who can see bookings rather than failing loudly.

This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

This is a correctness regression (invalid inputs now permitted by the public type/signature) introduced by the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the public `findMany` method from `InsightsBookingService` (replaced by `getBaseConditions()` returning `Prisma.Sql`). Any existing callers that still invoke `service.findMany(...)` would break at compile/runtime unless updated elsewhere, but the provided diff only shows test migration and does not show consumer migrations. The finding’s “no replacement” is overstated (there is a new `getBaseConditions`), but it is still an API-breaking change that requires coordinated updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] buildOrgAuthorizationCondition emits ("teamId" = ANY($1)) with an empty array parameter when the org has no child teams, which Postgres cannot type-infer. When findAllByParentId returns [], the generated Prisma.sql contains = ANY($1) bound to a JS empty array; Prisma serializes it as an untyped empty array literal and Postgres raises 'cannot determine type of empty array', turning the whole insights query into a 500 instead of the previous safe empty result (old code used teamId:{in:[]} which Prisma handles).

adjudication.rationale: In buildOrgAuthorizationCondition the SQL is built as Prisma.sql`("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)`, where teamIds is passed as a bound parameter (not an `ARRAY[]` literal). Given the expression context compares the `teamId` column, Postgres can infer the parameter type as the corresponding array type (e.g., int[]), and `= ANY($1)` with an empty array parameter evaluates to false rather than error. The diff alone does not show Prisma emitting an untyped empty array literal nor any code path that would force `ARRAY[]` without a cast.

A caller constructing the service with scope:'team' and no teamId passes the compiler; at runtime findByIdAndParentId({id: options.teamId}) receives undefined and the resulting Prisma query throws or silently matches nothing, where the previous InsightsBookingServiceOptions union (still exported and still used by buildOrgAuthorizationCondition/buildTeamAuthorizationCondition) rejected this shape at compile time.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` with `teamId?: number` and changes the constructor to accept this looser type (`options: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`). The service later uses `options.teamId` in `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` when calling `teamRepo.findByIdAndParentId({ id: options.teamId, parentId: options.orgId, ... })` with no runtime validation that `teamId` is defined for `scope === "team"`. This creates a real risk that a caller can pass `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` (now typechecks per the constructor signature) and `options.teamId` becomes `undefined`, leading to an invalid/erroneous query or unintended behavior. The prior discriminated-union options type would have prevented this shape at compile time.

A regression that re-fetches authorization conditions on every getAuthorizationConditions() call (e.g. the cache-check rewritten to assign before early-return) would no longer be caught by any test, silently reintroducing N+1 membership/team lookups per insights request; the deleted tests were the only assertions that the second call returns the cached conditions.

adjudication.rationale: The diff deletes the entire `describe("Caching")` block in `insightsBooking.integration-test.ts` (the only tests asserting that repeated calls return the same cached conditions), while the production service still implements caching via `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` and the `=== undefined` guard in `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()` in `insightsBooking.ts`. This isn’t a functional bug introduced by the diff, but it is a concrete test-coverage regression: cache behavior is no longer verified and a future regression in those guards would not be caught.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] buildTeamAuthorizationCondition omits the isTeamBooking:false branch when userIdsFromTeam is empty, but buildOrgAuthorizationCondition keeps its team branch even when teamIds is empty, leaving the two symmetric builders with divergent empty-set handling. The next maintainer adding a scope or copying one builder as a template inherits inconsistent assumptions about which branches are safe to drop, and the empty-teamIds org path (single ANY([]) condition) is exactly the branch whose behavior was not audited.

adjudication.rationale: In `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`, the code always includes `Prisma.sql`("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)`` even when `teamIds` could be an empty array (it is derived from `teamsFromOrg.map(...)` and there is no length check). By contrast, the optional user branch is explicitly skipped when `userIdsFromOrg.length === 0`, and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` similarly skips its user-id branch when empty. The diff does not show any explicit handling/tests for the `ANY([])` org path, so the reviewer’s concern about an unaudited empty-set edge case is diff-grounded, but it’s not verifiably a runtime/correctness defect from the diff alone.

Every existing consumer that called service.findMany(...) now gets a compile error or, worse, must hand-write `SELECT ... WHERE ${baseConditions}` raw SQL per call site, duplicating table/column knowledge outside the service; this work is not traceable to the stated intent and expands scope across the codebase.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the previously public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method from `InsightsBookingService` and replaces it with `getBaseConditions(): Promise<Prisma.Sql>` (see `insightsBooking.ts`). This is a breaking public API change: any existing callers using `service.findMany(...)` would no longer compile, and the new API only returns a SQL condition fragment rather than performing the query via Prisma. While this is not provably a runtime correctness bug from the diff alone (it may be intentional), it is a concrete, diff-grounded scope/architecture concern because it pushes query construction/execution responsibility outside the service.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] New exported type InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions (userId and orgId unconditionally required, teamId optional) is added without any requirement, and it silently replaces the validated InsightsBookingServiceOptions as the constructor input. The zod discriminated union insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema (lines 8-26) is now dead at this call path: callers can pass options that violate the union (e.g. scope 'team' with no teamId, orgId: undefined at runtime) and the service will build SQL against undefined values instead of failing validation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the constructor parameter from the zod-inferred `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` to a new exported `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` where `teamId` is optional regardless of `scope`, and the constructor simply assigns `this.options = options` (no `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema.parse(...)` is shown). This removes both compile-time discrimination (e.g., `scope: "team"` without `teamId` now type-checks) and any runtime validation at this call path. With invalid/undefined values, the service can build conditions using them (e.g., `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` uses `options.teamId` in repository lookup and later in `Prisma.sql`), or pass `undefined` into `isOrgOwnerOrAdmin` lookups, leading to incorrect behavior rather than failing fast.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Constructing the raw-SQL fragments inside getBaseConditions couples every caller to the exact table name and quoted column identifiers of BookingTimeStatusDenormalized, an invariant the service previously encapsulated via Prisma's typed where-input. Any future caller composing getBaseConditions() into a raw query must know the physical column names ("isTeamBooking", "eventParentId") and table name; a rename or dialect change (this SQL is Postgres-specific with = ANY) breaks every call site at runtime instead of compile time.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the typed Prisma `findMany` API with `getBaseConditions(): Prisma.Sql`, and the service now constructs raw SQL predicates with quoted physical column names (e.g., `Prisma.sql\`("userId" = ${...}) AND ("teamId" IS NULL)\``; filters use `"eventParentId"`, `"isTeamBooking"`, etc.) and Postgres-specific operators like `= ANY(...)`. With `findMany` removed, callers must now run their own raw query against the underlying table (as shown in the test using `$queryRaw` on `"BookingTimeStatusDenormalized"`), which reduces compile-time safety and increases coupling to the DB schema/dialect. The finding slightly overstates that `getBaseConditions` itself contains the table name (it doesn’t), but the overall coupling concern is directly created by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The entire 'Caching' describe block is deleted, removing all coverage for the caching behavior that still exists in the service (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions memoization in insightsBooking.ts). adjudication.rationale: The diff deletes the entire `describe("Caching")` block from `insightsBooking.integration-test.ts`, removing explicit test coverage that repeated calls return cached values. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The MembershipRole.array.includes check is rewritten to === comparisons with no requirement driving it — unrelated refactoring bundled into a raw-query conversion PR. Behavior is equivalent today, but the churn makes it harder to attribute this diff's intent in review/git-blame; if MembershipRole gains case variants the explicit === pair silently excludes them where includes() would have kept parity visible.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `([MembershipRole.OWNER, MembershipRole.ADMIN] as const).includes(membership.role)` to `(membership.role === MembershipRole.OWNER || membership.role === MembershipRole.ADMIN)` in `isOrgOwnerOrAdmin()`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getBaseConditions falls back to NOTHING_CONDITION when both inputs are null, changing the former semantics where an empty AND array meant 'no restriction'. Currently unreachable as a behavior change (buildAuthorizationConditions never returns null), but the branch encodes deny-by-default for a state that previously meant permissive; if a future scope returns null to mean 'unrestricted', this silently returns zero rows instead.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `getBaseConditions()` implementation, the final `else` returns `NOTHING_CONDITION` (Prisma.sql`1=0`) when both `authConditions` and `filterConditions` are falsy (both null) (see `getBaseConditions` in `insightsBooking.ts`). In the prior `findMany` approach, `AND: [authConditions, filterConditions].filter(...)` could theoretically produce an empty `AND: []`, which in Prisma where semantics is effectively no restriction. While the diff also shows `getAuthorizationConditions()` now always returns a `Prisma.Sql` (never `null`), making this path currently unreachable, the finding is correctly grounded that the new branch encodes deny-by-default for a state that would have been permissive before if null were ever used to represent “unrestricted”.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Prisma.sql expands interpolated arrays into a comma-separated parameter list, so `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))` renders as `= ANY($1, $2, $3)` which is invalid Postgres syntax, crashing every org/team-scope query with more than one member/team. The first org or team-scope insights request with 2+ teams/users throws a raw-query syntax error and returns a 500; the single-element integration test never exercises the multi-element path, so CI stays green.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes condition building from Prisma `WhereInput` objects to raw SQL fragments using `Prisma.sql`, and in org/team scopes it now emits `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))` / `("userId" = ANY(${userIds}))` where the interpolated value is a JS array (e.g. `teamIds`, `userIdsFromTeam`, `uniqueUserIds`). This is a risky/likely-invalid use with Prisma raw SQL because array interpolation may expand into multiple bind parameters rather than a single Postgres array parameter, which would make `ANY($1, $2, ...)` syntactically invalid. The integration tests were also rewritten to use `ANY(${[singleId]})` only, so they would not exercise the multi-element path that would trigger such a syntax error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The toEqual assertions compare Prisma.Sql fragments by string content, but the production code parameterizes `isTeamBooking` (rendering `$2`) while the tests expect the literal `= true`, and the combined-condition test writes filter-AND-auth in an order the code emits as auth-AND-filter, so the assertions cannot match. These test cases fail as written (or force a meaningless string-diff rewrite), so the suite does not actually verify the generated authorization SQL against a real query — a stand-in guard that validates textual form, not behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show `isTeamBooking` being parameterized (it is written as a SQL literal: `("isTeamBooking" = true)` / `= false`, not `${true}`), so the claimed `$2` vs `= true` mismatch is not supported. Also, the “combined-condition test” no longer asserts equality of auth/filter SQL strings at all: it calls `getBaseConditions()` and runs a real `$queryRaw ... WHERE ${baseConditions}` and asserts returned rows, so there is no filter-AND-auth textual order assertion to fail. While `toEqual` on `Prisma.Sql` may be brittle in general, the specific failure mechanisms described are not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The public method findMany was deleted and the return types of getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions changed from Prisma WhereInput to Prisma.Sql, breaking every existing caller that composed or executed these conditions via the Prisma client. Any call site outside this diff still calling service.findMany or passing the conditions to prisma.bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany now fails at type-check or, worse, receives a Prisma.Sql object a Prisma `where` cannot interpret, silently filtering nothing when duck-typed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does delete the previously available `findMany` method and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()`, and it changes `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` return types from `Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput` to `Prisma.Sql` (see `insightsBooking.ts`). This is an API-breaking change for any existing callers expecting to call `service.findMany(...)` or compose the returned conditions into a Prisma `where` object. However, the claim about callers “silently filtering nothing when duck-typed” is not verifiable from the diff, and whether there are any other call sites is outside what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions type replaces the zod-discriminated union at the constructor boundary, making userId and orgId required for every scope and dropping runtime validation of options entirely. A caller constructing the service with scope 'team' but no userId/orgId, or with an unvalidated string scope, no longer fails validation; the zod schema is retained but nothing enforces it, so the next caller passes malformed options that surface as a broken authorization condition instead of a 4xx.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the constructor to accept `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` (a plain TS type) instead of `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` (zod-inferred), but there is no runtime zod validation shown either before or after (no `schema.parse(...)` call), so the claim that runtime validation was “dropped” is not verifiable from this diff. Also, the finding says callers could omit `userId/orgId`, but the new type *requires* `userId` and `orgId` for all scopes (`InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`), so that specific regression is contradicted by the code. While `teamId` becoming optional for scope `team` could be a separate concern, it is not what the finding asserts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The service now emits hand-written, Postgres-dialect raw SQL with quoted camelCase identifiers, coupling the service to (a) the exact physical column names of BookingTimeStatusDenormalized and (b) Postgres-specific constructs (ANY), removing the database-agnostic and schema-map-safe layer Prisma previously provided. Any future column rename, @map, or driver change silently breaks every authorization query at runtime rather than at type-check; a staff reviewer should weigh whether raw SQL is needed here at all, since the previous WhereInput expressed the same conditions.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces Prisma `BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput` objects with hand-written SQL fragments via `Prisma.sql` throughout `InsightsBookingService` (e.g., `("userId" = ${...}) AND ("teamId" IS NULL)`, and `"userId" = ANY(${userIds})` in `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`/`buildTeamAuthorizationCondition`). This couples the logic to quoted physical column names and Postgres-specific constructs like `ANY`, whereas the previous implementation expressed the same logic using Prisma’s typed/mapper-aware `where` clauses. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/portability concern, but not an immediately verifiable runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition duplicate the same team-booking/user-booking OR-arm construction with hand-rolled reduce-based joining, a pattern now copied three times across the file (org, team, filter). The next condition variant (e.g. a third OR arm or a parenthesization fix) must be applied in three places; the drift already shows as inconsistent parenthesization between the org and filter reducers, and a precedence mistake in one copy is exactly the kind of authorization bug raw SQL invites.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce repeated, hand-rolled SQL-joining patterns via `reduce` in multiple places: `buildFilterConditions()` (AND-join), `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition()` (OR-join), and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition()` (OR-join). This is a maintainability/design concern created by the change: any future change to how conditions are combined/parenthesized would need to be replicated across these separate reducers, increasing drift risk. However, the finding’s claim of an already-present, verifiable precedence/parenthesization bug is not clearly demonstrated by the diff (each reducer wraps `acc` and `condition` in parentheses, and `getBaseConditions()` also wraps both sides), so it’s not a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The public exported method findMany was deleted and replaced by getBaseConditions, removing the only documented way callers consumed this service (Prisma findMany args API) without any adapter keeping the old call signature. Every existing caller of InsightsBookingService.findMany (routing/UI data layers not in this diff) fails to compile or, for dynamically-typed call sites, silently gets no data — the PR's stated intent was 'convert to Prisma.sql raw queries', but the iteration quietly changed the objective to a public API removal, an objective change with no explicit human acceptance recorded in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably removes the public method `findMany(findManyArgs: Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs)` from `InsightsBookingService` and replaces it with `getBaseConditions(): Promise<Prisma.Sql>` (see `insightsBooking.ts` where `findMany` is deleted and `getBaseConditions` added, and tests updated to use `$queryRaw`). There is no compatibility wrapper preserving the previous Prisma `findMany`-args API. Whether this is a compile-breaking defect for existing callers cannot be confirmed from this diff alone, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded public API breaking change that warrants explicit handling/acceptance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new hand-written InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions type duplicates the existing zod discriminated union insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema instead of deriving from it (z.infer), and the constructor silently switched its accepted type from the validated InsightsBookingServiceOptions to this parallel type. Two sources of truth for the options contract: when the zod schema is next tightened or a scope gains/loses a required field (e.g. teamId), this type drifts silently; worse, the constructor no longer receives the zod-validated type, so unvalidated option shapes now flow into buildAuthorizationConditions where an unrecognized shape falls through to the else branch returning NOTHING_CONDITION — the user silently sees an empty insights dashboard instead of a 4xx validation error.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a separate `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` type (with `teamId?: number`) alongside the existing `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema`/`InsightsBookingServiceOptions = z.infer<...>`, and the constructor signature changes from `options: InsightsBookingServiceOptions` to `options: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` while `this.options` remains typed as `InsightsBookingServiceOptions | null`. This creates two sources of truth and weakens the discriminated-union typing (e.g., `teamId` no longer required for `scope: "team"` at compile time), which can allow invalid shapes to reach `buildAuthorizationConditions()` and result in `NOTHING_CONDITION` (e.g., `teamId` undefined leading to `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` returning nothing). However, the claim about losing a 4xx validation error is not verifiable from the diff because neither version shows runtime zod parsing/validation in the constructor.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The entire Caching describe block (both the authorization-conditions cache test and the filter-conditions cache test) was deleted even though the caching implementation (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions in insightsBooking.ts) was retained. The cache behavior is now completely untested: a regression that re-queries conditions per call (or caches stale conditions across filter changes) would pass CI; deleting tests that guard still-present behavior is an objective change (from 'verify caching' to 'drop caching verification') that no human acceptance is recorded for.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the entire "describe('Caching')" block from insightsBooking.integration-test.ts (both cache tests), while the implementation still retains caching state (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions) and memoization logic in getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions in insightsBooking.ts. This is a concrete loss of coverage for behavior that still exists (conditions should be built once per instance), so regressions to the caching semantics would no longer be caught by CI, even though no functional defect is directly shown by the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The rewritten assertions compare getAuthorizationConditions output against the exact Prisma.sql fragment the implementation builds, string-for-string including quoting and ANY() formatting, rather than asserting any semantic property. The tests are now tautological mirrors of the implementation: any harmless refactor (reordering parentheses, changing ANY-array serialization, renaming quoting style) breaks five tests with no behavioral change, while a real authorization bug that is consistently reflected in both implementation and expected-SQL literal (e.g. swapping isTeamBooking true/false) passes CI — the previous Prisma-where-object assertions at least encoded intent independently of serialization.

adjudication.rationale: The diff rewrites multiple tests to assert exact `Prisma.sql` fragments (e.g. `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`("userId" = ${...}) AND ("teamId" IS NULL)`) and `ANY(${[...]})` forms) instead of higher-level intent/structure. This is diff-grounded and makes tests tightly coupled to implementation-specific SQL formatting/parenthesization/quoting, so harmless refactors to the SQL builder could break tests without behavioral change. It’s a test-quality/maintainability concern rather than a directly verifiable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The final else branch of getBaseConditions returning NOTHING_CONDITION is dead code: getAuthorizationConditions is typed Promise<Prisma.Sql> (non-nullable) and always returns a fragment, so authConditions is never null and the 'both null' path can never execute. It also silently encodes a semantic that differs from the removed findMany, where authConditions was unconditionally ANDed and an empty AND array meant 'no restriction'; a future reader extending filter nullability could rely on this branch believing 'both absent = see nothing' when the historical intent for absent auth was never defined here.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `getAuthorizationConditions()` is typed as `Promise<Prisma.Sql>` and `buildAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` fragment (falling back to `NOTHING_CONDITION = Prisma.sql`1=0``), never `null`/`undefined`. Therefore in `getBaseConditions()`, `authConditions` is always truthy and the final `else { return NOTHING_CONDITION; }` branch is effectively unreachable (dead code) and potentially confusing to future maintainers. However, this does not create a runtime correctness bug given the current return types/logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The entire 'Caching' describe block (both cache tests) was deleted from the test file while the caching logic (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions memoization in insightsBooking.ts getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions) remains in the implementation, so the cache behavior is no longer asserted anywhere in this diff. A future regression that breaks or removes memoization (e.g., re-querying memberships on every call, or returning a stale/wrong cached condition) passes the suite silently; previously the deleted 'should cache authorization conditions'/'should cache filter conditions' tests caught this by calling the getter twice and asserting the second result equaled the first.

adjudication.rationale: In the test diff, the entire `describe("Caching")` block (both cache tests) was removed from `insightsBooking.integration-test.ts` (the section starting right after the combined filter-condition test). In the implementation (`insightsBooking.ts`), memoization still exists via `cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions` guarded by `if (this.cachedAuthConditions === undefined)` and `if (this.cachedFilterConditions === undefined)` in `getAuthorizationConditions()` / `getFilterConditions()`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The org-scope and team-scope authorization tests verify the produced SQL only by string-mirror equality against a hand-copied duplicate of the implementation's template literal, and never execute it — the ONLY test that runs the conditions through prisma.$queryRaw (the renamed getBaseConditions test) exercises solely the scope:'user' path, so the `("userId" = ANY(${[...]}))` / `("teamId" = ANY(${[...]}))` constructs are never executed against Postgres. If Prisma's sql tag expands the passed array into multiple placeholders (its documented behavior for arrays, producing `ANY($1, $2, ...)` which is invalid Postgres syntax — correct usage is a single array param or Prisma.join), every org- and team-scoped Insights query would crash at runtime with a syntax/prepared-statement error, while these tests still pass because the test's mirrored template produces the identical (broken) SQL string; the mirror also means any precedence bug duplicated in both the impl and the test literal is invisible.

adjudication.rationale: Diff changes org/team/user authorization and filter conditions from Prisma `WhereInput` objects to raw `Prisma.sql` fragments, and the tests were updated to assert `toEqual(Prisma.sql`...`)` with literals that largely duplicate the implementation (e.g., org/team scopes expect `"teamId" = ANY(${[...]})` / `"userId" = ANY(${[...]})`). Those tests do not execute the generated SQL against Postgres; the only added execution path shown is the renamed `getBaseConditions` test which builds conditions and runs `$queryRaw`, but it appears to exercise only the `scope: "user"` branch (which returns `("userId" = ...) AND ("teamId" IS NULL)` and does not use `ANY(...)`). Therefore, the org/team `ANY(${teamIds})` / `ANY(${userIdsFromTeam})` constructs introduced in `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` / `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` are not validated by running a real query in the test suite as shown. The finding’s claim of a specific Prisma array-expansion bug is not verifiable from the diff alone, but the test weakness (mirror-equality + no execution for org/team SQL) is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The rewritten scope:'user' assertion compares against a template literal duplicated from the implementation rather than querying with the conditions, so it verifies textual identity, not filter semantics. A change that alters parameter binding (e.g., binding the wrong column order or swapping userId/teamId values) that happens to produce identical text in both copies passes; the semantic guarantee now rests entirely on the single getBaseConditions raw-execution test, which covers only this one scope's shape.

adjudication.rationale: In the updated integration tests, several assertions (including the scope:"user" authorization condition) now do `expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`...`)` with SQL fragments that mirror the implementation in `buildAuthorizationConditions()` (e.g., `return Prisma.sql`("userId" = ${this.options.userId}) AND ("teamId" IS NULL)``). This tightly couples the test to the exact SQL construction rather than validating behavior via executing a query, so it mainly checks structural/identity equivalence of the `Prisma.sql` object. The only semantic execution added is the `getBaseConditions` test using `$queryRaw`, and it covers just one combined scenario, leaving other scopes/branches (org/team, empty arrays, etc.) not semantically exercised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The getBaseConditions test suite in this diff covers only the both-conditions-present path; the new else-branches in getBaseConditions (filter-only, and both-null returning NOTHING_CONDITION) are never triggered by any test in the diff. A regression in the branch selection (e.g., returning null instead of NOTHING_CONDITION when both are null, causing the raw WHERE clause to receive a non-SQL value and the $queryRaw to fail or match nothing) would not be caught; previously the filter-less caching test at least exercised the filter-null path through the old findMany.

adjudication.rationale:
In `InsightsBookingService.getBaseConditions()` new branching logic was introduced:
- `if (authConditions && filterConditions)`
- `else if (authConditions)`
- `else if (filterConditions)`
- `else` returning `NOTHING_CONDITION`

The updated integration test `describe("getBaseConditions")` only exercises the first branch (both auth + filter present) by constructing the service with `filters: { eventTypeId: ... }` and then querying with `WHERE ${baseConditions}`. No test in the diff constructs the service without `filters` (so that `getFilterConditions()` returns `null`) to exercise the `else if (authConditions)` path. That’s a specific, diff-grounded gap in coverage for the new base-condition composition.

However, the finding’s claim about “filter-only” and “both-null” branches being triggerable is overstated: per this diff `getAuthorizationConditions()` returns `Prisma.Sql` and `buildAuthorizationConditions()` returns `NOTHING_CONDITION` rather than `null`, so `authConditions` is never `null` and those branches are effectively unreachable in the current code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Neither org-scope test covers the empty-list branches the implementation explicitly guards (userIdsFromOrg.length === 0 in buildOrgAuthorizationCondition, userIdsFromTeam.length === 0 in buildTeamAuthorizationCondition), even though the diff restructured exactly those branches. If the empty-list guard is dropped or mis-edited (e.g., the condition pushed unconditionally with an empty array), tests still pass because every fixture populates members; the resulting SQL (`userId = ANY(empty)` matching no personal bookings vs. previously `userId: {in: []}` semantics) is unverified against real data.

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds explicit empty-list guards before appending the personal-bookings OR branch: `if (userIdsFromOrg.length > 0) { ... ANY(${uniqueUserIds}) ... }` in `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` and `if (userIdsFromTeam.length > 0) { ... ANY(${userIdsFromTeam}) ... }` in `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition`. The integration tests updated in this PR only assert SQL for cases where fixtures produce non-empty member lists (e.g., org/team scope tests build user/team arrays with at least the creator and added users), and there is no test exercising the `length === 0` paths. So the advisory about missing coverage for these newly restructured branches is diff-grounded and actionable, but it’s not a verifiable defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] buildOrgAuthorizationCondition unconditionally emits `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))` even when teamIds is empty, producing invalid/untyped empty-array SQL where the old `{ teamId: { in: [] } }` was a valid always-false condition. An org whose orgId has no child teams (or where findAllByParentId returns empty) causes the Prisma raw query to fail at runtime with a Postgres parameter-type/ARRAY error instead of returning zero rows, turning an authorized-but-empty org into a 500 on every insights request.

adjudication.rationale: In `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`, the first condition is always `Prisma.sql`("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})) AND ("isTeamBooking" = true)`` with `teamIds` derived directly from `teamsFromOrg.map(...)` and never guarded for the empty-org case. If `findAllByParentId` returns no teams, `teamIds` is `[]` and this raw-SQL path now depends on how Prisma/PG binds an empty JS array for `ANY($1)`. The previous Prisma `where: { teamId: { in: [] } }` reliably behaved as an always-false filter without SQL typing concerns. This diff therefore introduces a real edge-case risk of runtime failure (or at minimum incorrect handling) for authorized orgs with zero child teams.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Constructor parameter type changed from the zod-validated InsightsBookingServiceOptions to a hand-written InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions structurally looser than the discriminated union, and the schema is never parsed at the boundary. Callers can now pass { scope: "team", userId, orgId } with a undefined/wrongly-typed teamId through type-asserted call sites; buildTeamAuthorizationCondition then interpolates undefined into `("teamId" = ${options.teamId})`, yielding `"teamId" = NULL` which matches no rows — an authorization condition that silently returns NOTHING instead of failing fast at the boundary.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the constructor still validates options at the boundary: `this.options = insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema.parse(options);` (insightsBooking.ts). Even though the constructor parameter type was widened to `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` with an optional `teamId?: number`, any `{ scope: "team" }` call missing/invalid `teamId` will throw during `parse`, not flow through to `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` and interpolate `undefined` into `Prisma.sql`. Therefore the claimed silent NOTHING behavior from `("teamId" = ${options.teamId})` cannot occur given the shown code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only test asserting cached conditions behave identically across repeat calls was deleted while the caching fields cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions remain live logic. A future regression in the memoization (e.g. caching a null filter then never rebuilding when filters change) would be invisible; this diff removed the only guard while keeping the mechanism, making the next change to buildFilterConditions riskier.

adjudication.rationale: The diff deletes the entire `describe("Caching")` block in `insightsBooking.integration-test.ts` that previously asserted repeat calls to `getAuthorizationConditions()`/`getFilterConditions()` return cached results. Meanwhile, the service still contains live memoization logic via `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` (now `Prisma.Sql` / `Prisma.Sql | null`) and the `if (this.cachedX === undefined) { this.cachedX = await ... }` pattern remains. Removing these tests reduces coverage specifically for the caching/memoization mechanism retained in `InsightsBookingService`, making regressions in that logic harder to detect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] buildTeamAuthorizationCondition interpolates userIdsFromTeam directly into `("userId" = ANY(${userIdsFromTeam}))` with the empty case only guarded by the if, so the non-empty path with a single-element list is fine but the corresponding Prisma.sql fragment template is duplicated from buildOrgAuthorizationCondition with inverted AND/OR logic — drift between the two copies (AND for org, OR join wrapper) is already present and one wrong edit flips authorization scope. The parallel hand-maintained raw-SQL builders mean the next authorization change (e.g. adding a role filter) must be edited in two places with opposite boolean joins; a mistake silently widens or narrows who can see bookings rather than failing loudly.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows both `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` building two optional branches (team bookings vs user bookings) and combining them with `OR` via the same `reduce` pattern; there is no “inverted AND/OR logic” drift present in the code as changed. The `ANY(${userIdsFromTeam})` fragment is only constructed when `userIdsFromTeam.length > 0`, so the empty-array case is guarded. While there is some duplicated raw-SQL-building structure, the finding’s claim of an already-present logic inversion/bug isn’t verifiable from the diff.
